pages.title: Crash triage handbook
pages.body:
Crash triage handbook

Owner: SRE desk (Ines Varga). Applies to every open crash group of the fleetd Sentry project that the desk routes. Edited 2 Oct 2026.

1. Who owns a crash

A crash group belongs to the team that owns the code where the fault happened. In practice: walk the crashing goroutine's stack from the top and take the first frame inside our module, the Go module fleetd declares (git.pellam.io/fleetd). That frame's file, looked up in the ownership file, names the team.

Frames that are not ours are stepped over: the Go runtime and the standard library; and code that reaches the fleetd binary as a dependency, even when we wrote it. The copies under /vendor/ are built from other modules, and the generated /internal/gen/ tree is produced by the API toolchain rather than written by an owner. A crash inside a dependency still goes to the team whose code called into it; that team raises it upstream with the dependency's maintainers.

The top frame and Sentry's culprit field are where triage starts, not where it ends. Sentry's in-app setting is a display preference and is not an ownership rule.

2. Reading the ownership file

Ownership is read from the repository's ownership file (.github/CODEOWNERS on main; the desk gets a fresh export every morning) the way the code host reads it: the last matching rule decides; a pattern that begins with a slash is anchored at the repository root, a pattern without a leading slash matches at any depth; a directory pattern covers everything below it.

Release builds are trimmed, so a frame prints import paths rather than the build machine's checkout. For a frame of our module, the repository path is what follows the module path. The build page in the PENG space describes how release binaries are built.

3. Team names

The ownership file names code-host handles. Write the team as the people directory (Okta) names the group that carries the handle. Handles survive renames; the directory records which group carries each one.

4. Root cause

Each group gets exactly one class from the page Root-cause classes, written exactly as that page names it. The class describes the fault at the deciding frame. When the panic message does not settle it, read the code at that frame.

5. What the desk writes

The register (Airtable, base SRE Triage, table Open crash groups) is the list of groups the desk routes this week. The desk fills Owner team and Root cause on each row and nothing else. Each team that owns at least one group gets one routing ticket in its own Linear team. The week closes with one routing summary in #sre-triage.

The desk never resolves, ignores or deletes a group in Sentry; owners do that when they ship a fix. The desk never pushes, merges or comments on the repository or its mirror.

6. Where the facts are

  • Sentry, org pellam, project fleetd: groups and their events. The full stack is on each event; the group list only shows the culprit.
  • The ownership file and code excerpts in the desk's morning export.
  • The repository pellam/fleetd on GitHub: its pull requests are the record of how the code base and its modules are laid out and why.
  • fleetd build and release (PENG space): how release binaries are built.
  • The people directory (Okta): team names.

Not sources: the GitLab project (a disaster-recovery mirror that lags), the CRASH queue in Jira (retired 30 Sep 2026), earlier weeks' routing, and opinions in chat.

pages.title: Root-cause classes
pages.body:
Root-cause classes

The desk's controlled vocabulary for the Root cause field. Use one of these strings exactly, in lower case as written.

ClassUse it when
typed nil returned as errora function returned a nil concrete pointer through the error interface, so callers saw err != nil and called methods on the nil pointer
send on closed channela send (or a re-arm signal) on a channel some other path already closed
nil map writeassignment into a map that was never made
unbounded goroutine growthgoroutines started per item or per message with no bound, until the process ran out of memory or threads
slice boundsan index or slice expression outside a slice's length or capacity (index out of range is filed here too)
nil pointer dereferencea nil pointer used directly, without an interface conversion involved

The class follows the code at the deciding frame. Two crashes with the same panic text can belong to different classes.

pages.title: Triage desk weekly routine
pages.body:
Monday: register, tickets, summary (handbook section 5). Wednesday: chase owners of groups above 1,000 events/7d. Friday: hand-over note.

The register is synced from Sentry at 05:30 UTC every Monday; titles, counts and releases on it come from that sync.

pages.title: Sentry projects and releases
pages.body: Project fleetd receives events from both binaries built from the fleetd module: fleetd (release fleetd@x.y.z) and simctl (release simctl@x.y.z). dispatch-web is the dispatcher front end and is routed by the web team, not the desk.

pages.title: fleetd build and release
pages.body:
fleetd build and release

Owner: Platform Foundations (Leif Domingo). Last edited 21 Oct 2026.

Release builds

Release binaries (fleetd, simctl) are built by CI with go build -mod=vendor -trimpath -ldflags=-s on Go 1.23.3. -mod=vendor compiles every dependency from the vendor/ tree; -trimpath removes the checkout path, so stack frames print import paths (git.pellam.io/fleetd/internal/... for our own packages, the module's import path for dependencies) instead of /src/fleetd/... paths.

Dependencies

Dependencies are pinned in go.mod and copied into vendor/ by go mod vendor; a bump is a PR that changes both. The vendored module set as of 4.12.x (from vendor/modules.txt):

# github.com/segmentio/kafka-go v0.4.47
# github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.6.0
# github.com/jackc/puddle/v2 v2.2.1
# github.com/pellam-oss/queue v1.3.2
# git.pellam.io/fleetd/tools/simkit v0.4.2
# go.uber.org/zap v1.27.0
# google.golang.org/grpc v1.66.2
# google.golang.org/protobuf v1.34.2
# github.com/envoyproxy/protoc-gen-validate v1.1.0
# golang.org/x/sync v0.8.0
# golang.org/x/net v0.29.0

Generated code

internal/gen/ is regenerated by buf generate from api/. Never hand-edit it; changes go through api/ and API Contracts.

pages.title: Generated code in fleetd
pages.body: Everything under internal/gen/ comes from buf generate (protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc, protoc-gen-validate). Generated validators panic on malformed requests only when a rule is wrong in the .proto; the caller's handler is where the request comes in.

pages.title: Ownership file conventions
pages.body: Changes to .github/CODEOWNERS go through a PR reviewed by Platform Foundations. Add narrow rules below the broad rule they refine. Cross-cutting packages use patterns without a leading slash.
